title: Service Boundaries Design
description: Design proper service boundaries using high cohesion, low coupling, data ownership, and API design principles.

data.text: Good service boundaries are the foundation of a healthy microservices architecture. The goal is high cohesion (related functionality stays together) and low coupling (services depend on each other as little as possible).

terms.definition: How closely related the responsibilities within a service are.
How much one service depends on another.
The principle that each service owns its data exclusively.
The practice of designing service interfaces that are stable and evolvable.

data.text: High cohesion means related functionality is grouped together. Low coupling means services depend on each other minimally. These principles guide service boundary design.

items: Single Responsibility: Each service has one reason to change
Data Ownership: Each service owns its data exclusively
Explicit Interfaces: Communicate through well-defined APIs
Loose Coupling: Minimize dependencies between services
High Cohesion: Keep related functionality together

data.text: Each service should own its data. Other services should access data through APIs, not through direct database access. This prevents tight coupling through shared databases.

items: Splitting by technical layer instead of business capability
Creating god services that do too much
Creating nano services that are too fine-grained

data.title: Exercise: Design Service Boundaries
data.description: Design service boundaries for a library management system (books, members, loans, reservations).
steps: Propose services with high cohesion and low coupling
Define data ownership for each service
data.expectedOutcome: A service design document with boundaries, data ownership, and APIs

items.question: How do you know if a boundary is wrong?
items.answer: If services change together frequently, the boundary is likely wrong. High cohesion means changes are contained.

items.question: Can services share a database?
items.answer: Technically yes, but it creates tight coupling. Each service should own its data.

items.question: What is the right size for a service?
items.answer: A service should map to a business capability. Too big means low cohesion; too small means too many network calls.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Design for high cohesion and low coupling
Each service owns its data exclusively
APIs should be versioned, documented, and stable
data.takeaway: Good boundaries come from understanding the business domain and applying cohesion/coupling principles.
